stem:
In the diagram, triangle ABC has point D on BC with AD perpendicular to BC, and point M the midpoint of BC.

Which segment is an altitude of triangle ABC?

options.text: AD, because it is perpendicular to side BC.
AM, because it joins A to a point on BC.
AD, used only as a length in an area calculation, not as an altitude of triangle ABC.
BC, because it is the longest side labelled in the diagram.

teacher.key_rationale: An altitude from A to BC is the perpendicular segment from A to BC, which is AD. AM meets BC without the perpendicular condition. Stretching AD into an area formula for another triangle, or picking the longest side, miss the altitude hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Triangle ABC with perpendicular AD to BC and median AM; learner picks the altitude.
